confirmed.authored: ["aquatic"] — stored at record level, so creatureTraitsOf() applies it to every Swimming Animal
confirmed.textSays: "Choose if you are aquatic or water-dwelling. — Aquatic: You gain the aquatic trait and you have a swim Speed of 30 feet. — Water-dwelling: You can hold your breath underwater for 10 minutes before needing air…"
confirmed.why:
CONFIRMED — could not refute. The printed text (public/core-descriptions.json, heritages/swimming-animal) reads "Choose if you are aquatic or water-dwelling. - **Aquatic:** You gain the aquatic trait and you have a swim Speed of 30 feet... - **Water-dwelling:** You can hold your breath underwater for 10 minutes before needing air." The words "You gain the aquatic trait" appear ONLY inside the Aquatic branch, behind an explicit "Choose if", and the same sentence defines the trait as "you breathe water but not air" — flatly incompatible with the water-dwelling branch's "hold your breath... before needing air". So the trait must not apply to a water-dwelling Swimming Animal.

The authored record (scripts/data/effect-backfill.json -> public/core.json) carries the choice as `effectChoices.aquatic-or-water-dwelling` AND a sibling record-level `grantsCreatureTraits: ["aquatic"]`.

Four refutation routes tried, all failed:
1. Reader is not choice-aware: creatureTraitsOf (src/rules/derive.ts:2213) gathers grantors via heritageRecords (derive.ts:1133), which maps c.heritageId/c.secondHeritageId straight to db.heritages and never consults BuildState.effectChoices. Every Swimming Animal gets aquatic.
2. Field doc does not license it: src/rules/types.ts:863 defines grantsCreatureTraits as "CREATURE TRAITS the record adds to the character... these are ACQUIRED on top" — unconditional.
3. Not a wording/placement difference: EffectGrant (types.ts:1210) has no creature-trait lane at all (grantsCreatureTraits has only 3 code hits, none per-option), so the trait genuinely cannot currently be attached to the branch that earns it. Real engine gap, not an equivalent encoding.
4. No owner ruling: docs/gold-set-answers.md has nothing on swimming-animal or aquatic; Q6 (line 52) only says acquired creature traits should be recorded on the sheet, which concerns surfacing, not conditioning.

Ground truth corroborates: Foundry's rule elements at .import-src/pf2e/packs/pf2e/heritages/awakened-animal/swimming-animal.json gate it as {"add":["aquatic"],"key":"ActorTraits","predicate":["swimming-animal:aquatic"]}. The record even contradicts itself — its own option label says "Aquatic (gain the aquatic trait; swim Speed 30 ft)", acknowledging the trait belongs to one branch while grantsCreatureTraits hands it to both.

Separate second defect on the same record (out of scope for this claim): the water-dwelling option's grant carries only speeds.swim = 20, missing the land Speed 20 ft its own label and the text ("if you can move on land, you have base Speed of 20 feet") promise.

confirmed.why:
CONFIRMED — I could not refute it.

PRINTED TEXT (identical in two independent copies: the AoN mirror `C:\wonderers guide\aon-2e-archive\data\by-category\feat\feat-4203.json`, Rage of Elements pg. 23, and the app's own `C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\public\core-descriptions.json`): "You also gain the elemental trait and the trait of your chosen element."

That sentence grants TWO traits. The authored value carries one — `grantsCreatureTraits: ["elemental"]`, in both `C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\public\core.json` and the durable overlay `C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\scripts\data\effect-backfill.json`. The specific words the value fails to cover are "and the trait of your chosen element".

FOUR REFUTATIONS TRIED, ALL FAILED:

1. "The element trait arrives from another record." No. `creatureTraitsOf` (`C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\derive.ts:2214-2238`) is the single reader, and it collects only `grantsCreatureTraits` off heritages, feats, owned class features and invested items. I scanned every record in core.json carrying that field (40 of them): not one grants air/earth/fire/metal/water/wood. A kineticist's element never becomes a creature trait anywhere in the app.

2. "The field's doc comment narrows it." It widens it, if anything — `C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\types.ts:854-863` defines the field as "CREATURE TRAITS the record adds to the character" and justifies it with "a creature trait changes what can target you". An element trait is exactly that (a fire elemental's creature traits are elemental + fire), so it is squarely in-lane.

3. "The owner already ruled this contextual." No such ruling. `docs/gold-set-answers.md` never mentions this feat; Q6 says only "Record acquired creature traits on the sheet". The nearest thing is the CONTEXTUAL exclusion in `C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\scripts\author-creature-traits.mjs` (which deliberately skips "the appropriate trait"/"the opposing trait" and PRINTS them "so they are not silently dropped") — and this feat was never routed through it. Its regex `\byou (?:also )?gain the ((?:[a-z]+)(?: and [a-z]+)?) traits?\b` terminates at the first "trait", captured "elemental", and never saw the second clause. A silent truncation, not a decision.

4. "Which element is unknowable, so one trait is all that can be authored." Fails on the facts. The feat's own prerequisite is "exactly one kinetic element", and the app already computes it: `elementTraitsOf(build, level)` in `C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\kineticElements.ts:79` returns the bare element name off the gate picks. The record even already carries a resolved six-option choice (`effectChoices` id `elemental-apotheosis-element`, air/earth/fire/metal/water/wood).

CAVEAT ON THE FIX — the claim names the right defect but the wrong field. `grantsCreatureTraits` is a flat `string[]`; writing "fire" into it would give fire to every character holding the feat. Neither escape route exists today: `EffectGrant` (`src/rules/types.ts:1210-1239`, the shape an effectChoices option confers) has no creature-trait member, and `creatureTraitsOf` never reads chosen effects. Closing this needs an engine change — either teach `creatureTraitsOf` to fold in `elementTraitsOf`, or add a creature-traits member to `EffectGrant` and hang it on the six existing options — not an authoring edit.

SCOPE NOTE (found while checking, same regex truncation): `heritages/aiuvarin` is authored `["elf"]` against "You gain the elf trait, the aiuvarin trait, and low-light vision", and `heritages/dromaar` is authored `["orc"]` against "You gain the orc trait, the dromaar trait". Both missing traits are flat literals with no choice involved, so unlike this feat those two are pure authoring defects fixable immediately. `feats/celestial-form`, `feats/fiendish-form` and `feats/celestial-rebirth` share the same dropped-second-clause shape but their second trait is a genuinely open pick.

CONFIRMED — could not refute. `deity-champion`'s `grantsCreatureTraits: ["holy"]` is an unconditional grant of a trait the printed text makes a three-way conditional.

WORDS CONTRADICTED (from public/core-descriptions.json → classFeatures["deity-champion"].d, "Sanctification" section, Player Core 2):
1. "If you \"can be\" holy or unholy according to your deity's sanctification entry, you make that choice" — the trait is a player choice, not a fixed grant.
2. "If the deity lists \"none,\" you can choose only options that don't require the holy or unholy trait." — a champion of a "none" deity acquires NO sanctification trait; the record hands them holy.
3. "**Unholy:** You gain the unholy trait and add that trait to any Strikes you make." — the unholy branch grants unholy, never holy. The same paragraph adds "If you are holy or unholy and gain the opposing trait in some way, you lose the previous trait until you atone," so putting holy on an unholy champion is not a harmless extra, it is the opposing trait.

WHY IT REALLY FIRES (not a wording quibble): creatureTraitsOf (C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\derive.ts:2213-2238) folds grantsCreatureTraits in for every owned class feature with no gate on any choice; deity-champion is a level-1 feature in classes.champion.features, so EVERY champion owns it. Sole consumer is C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\sheet\DetailsTab.tsx:75, which applies no filter. Result: an Unholy champion and a "none"-sanctification champion both display "holy" as an acquired creature trait.

THE CORRECT VALUE IS ALREADY IN THE SAME RECORD: deity-champion carries choice { flag: "sanctification", kind: "array", options: holy / unholy / none }, and sanctificationOf(c) (derive.ts:1193-1197) already reads that pick off c.effectPicks. Nothing wires it to the trait lane, so the authored constant overrides a value the app can compute correctly.

REFUTATIONS I TRIED AND THEY FAILED:
- Field doc comment (src/rules/types.ts:852-863) reads "CREATURE TRAITS the record adds to the character" and mandates reading through creatureTraitsOf — it defines an unconditional add, not a menu of possibilities, so it does not rescue the value.
- Owner rulings: no ruling on champion sanctification anywhere in docs/gold-set-answers.md (grep for champion/sanctif/unholy returns only two unrelated aura/class lines); Q6 only says record acquired traits on the sheet.
- Neighbouring-clause defence fails in reverse: the reviewer quoted the governing clause; it is the AUTHORING that read only the neighbouring "**Holy:**" branch.
- Internal consistency check: deity-champion is the ONLY classFeatures entry among the 40 grantsCreatureTraits rows; every other row is an unconditional identity grant (heritages, undead/vampire dedications). The cleric's own sanctification feature carries no such field.

ROOT CAUSE: C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\scripts\author-creature-traits.mjs:34 runs /\byou (?:also )?gain the ((?:[a-z]+)(?: and [a-z]+)?) traits?\b/i over the full description and takes .match()'s FIRST hit — the "**Holy:**" paragraph. The "**Unholy:**" paragraph is later in the same text and is never examined. Lines 25-32 of that script explicitly name this failure mode ("the opposing trait (deity-cleric, Mortal Herald Dedication) — holy or unholy, per the deity… They need a choice-driven grant, which is a different lane") and exclude the cleric via the CONTEXTUAL set; champion escaped only because its text spells the literal word "holy" in one branch instead of saying "the opposing trait".

FIX SHAPE: drop the static ["holy"] row and drive the trait off the existing sanctification pick (the "choice-driven grant" lane the script header already anticipated), so holy/unholy/none each produce the right trait.

confirmed.why:
CONFIRMED — I could not refute it.

DECISIVE WORDS. public/core-descriptions.json, heritages.undine contains two separate grant clauses. The first ("You gain the undine trait, in addition to the traits from your ancestry") is what the authored value covers. The second is: "You gain a swim Speed of 10 feet and the amphibious trait." That clause grants a creature trait the authored value omits. Authored value (scripts/data/effect-backfill.json, row category=heritages id=undine field=grantsCreatureTraits) is ["undine"].

REFUTATIONS TESTED AND RULED OUT:

1. "The record's own traits:['amphibious','undine'] covers it." FALSE. creatureTraitsOf (src/rules/derive.ts:2213) seeds only from db.ancestries[c.ancestryId]?.traits, then iterates grantors (heritageRecords, feats, classFeatures, invested items) reading ONLY rec?.grantsCreatureTraits (line 2236). A heritage's own `traits` array is never read by it. Undine is versatile (ancestryId: null), so no ancestry can supply amphibious. DetailsTab.tsx:75 -> :413 is the sole consumer and renders exactly that list, so an undine character's Traits row shows "Undine" and not "Amphibious".

2. "The field's doc comment makes ['undine'] correct." FALSE — it makes it wrong. src/rules/types.ts:863 defines grantsCreatureTraits as "CREATURE TRAITS the record adds to the character" and states: "Read through creatureTraitsOf, never off a record directly, so every consumer sees the same set." Amphibious is added to the character by the printed text, so it belongs in the field.

3. "The owner already ruled." FALSE. docs/gold-set-answers.md line 52, Q6: "Record acquired creature traits on the sheet (the Details tab already carries tags)." No exemption for undine, amphibious, or for traits duplicated into a record's `traits` array. Grep of that file for "amphibious" and "undine" returns nothing.

4. "Amphibious is carried by a different lane." FALSE. breathesWater (derive.ts:2192) is a separate boolean; undine does not set it. The only other place a heritage's `traits` array is read is FeatsTab.tsx:242, which renders the heritage CARD's AoN trait pills — a different surface, not the character's creature-trait set.

5. "The siblings differ." FALSE. aquatic-elf and tidepool-dragonet carry the identical grant wording and BOTH author grantsCreatureTraits:["amphibious"] in effect-backfill.json. Precedent is against undine.

ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED. scripts/author-creature-traits.mjs:33 uses a non-global regex consumed by a single .match():
  const RE = /\byou (?:also )?gain the ((?:[a-z]+)(?: and [a-z]+)?) traits?\b/i;
It takes the FIRST clause only, and its shape accepts only "gain the X trait" / "gain the X and Y traits". Undine's second clause is unreachable (no /g) and unmatchable anyway (the intervening "a swim Speed of 10 feet and" breaks the pattern). The siblings each have only one such clause, which is why they came out right.

SCOPE — the same regex under-authored two more heritages via the comma-list form ("You gain the orc trait, the dromaar trait, and low-light vision"):
  - heritages/aiuvarin: authored ["elf"], text also grants aiuvarin (record traits: ["aiuvarin"])
  - heritages/dromaar: authored ["orc"], text also grants dromaar (record traits: ["dromaar"])
A fourth scan hit, classFeatures/deity-champion ("previous"), is a false positive.

FIX: heritages/undine grantsCreatureTraits -> ["undine","amphibious"]; aiuvarin -> ["elf","aiuvarin"]; dromaar -> ["orc","dromaar"]. Edit scripts/data/effect-backfill.json (the only lane that survives npm run data), and make RE global/multi-clause in scripts/author-creature-traits.mjs so the miss cannot recur.

CONFIRMED — I tried each of the usual refutations and none survived.

1. The text is real, not a paraphrase. `C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/public/core-descriptions.json` → `feats["celestial-rebirth"].d` and the pristine archive at `C:/wonderers guide/aon-2e-archive/data/by-category/feat/feat-7344.json` agree word for word: "You gain the celestial and holy traits, **as well as the agathion, angel, archon, or azata trait**, depending on whose ranks you are joining." The AoN markdown links all four (agathion/angel/archon/azata) to `/Traits.aspx?ID=…`, so they are creature traits, not flavour. The authored value in `C:/trying ai 2/pf2e codex/scripts/data/effect-backfill.json` (index 6729, mirrored into `public/core.json`) is `["celestial","holy"]` — two of the three clauses. Not a neighbouring-clause misread: the missing trait is in the *same sentence* as the two that were captured, joined by "as well as".

2. The doc comment does not license the omission. `src/rules/types.ts:855-863` defines the field as "CREATURE TRAITS the record adds to the character", explicitly "Not cosmetic. A creature trait changes what can target you… Your ancestry's own traits are the baseline; these are ACQUIRED on top". The chosen lineage trait is exactly an acquired creature trait, so the field's own definition covers it rather than excusing it.

3. No owner ruling covers it. `docs/gold-set-answers.md:52` Q6 rules "**Record acquired creature traits on the sheet**" — that pushes toward the claim, not away. Neither `gold-set-answers.md`, `gold-set-final.md`, `gold-set-review.md`, `gold-set-open-questions.md` nor `CLAUDE.md` mentions Celestial Rebirth at all, and nothing scopes Q6 to non-chosen traits.

4. No alternative route carries it. `creatureTraitsOf` (`src/rules/derive.ts:2213-2238`) builds its grantor list from heritages, feats, class features and invested items and reads exactly `for (const t of rec?.grantsCreatureTraits ?? []) add(t, 'granted', rec?.name)` — a static array per record, no choice input. `src/sheet/DetailsTab.tsx:75` + `:413` is the only surface, and it renders that function's output verbatim. Grepping `src/` for `reatureTrait` returns only those three files, so there is no second lane.

5. The `celestialTrait` choice really is echo-only. Grep for `celestialTrait` across `src/` returns **zero** matches. The record's choice (`core.json` → `feats["celestial-rebirth"].choice`, `kind:'array'`, four bare `{value,label}` options) sets no `ownsFeature` and no per-option `grant`, and `EffectGrant` (`types.ts:1211-1238`) has no creature-trait field at all. The only three generic consumers of a `choice.flag` are `weaponFromChoiceFlag` (`build.ts:3967`), the `{choice}` note placeholder (`derive.ts:2837`) and `fromChoiceFlag` (`derive.ts:2963`) — and this feat has no `note`, so none of them fires. The pick is stored and read by nothing.

Scope note for whoever fixes it: the correct fix is NOT appending a fourth string to `grantsCreatureTraits` (the trait is one-of-four, player-chosen). It needs a choice→creature-trait route — either a per-option `grantsCreatureTraits` honoured by `creatureTraitsOf`, or a `grantsCreatureTraitsFromChoiceFlag` field. Two sibling records are in the same shape and worth checking in the same pass: `mummy-dedication` (`["mummy","undead"]`, flag `terrain`) and `werecreature-dedication` (`["beast","werecreature"]`, flag `choice`).

The codebase already has the exact idiom (`saveShift(CF2F, 'fortitude', 'on any Fortitude save')`, used ~40 times), and **two lines above this very row** the identical shape is authored correctly: `'items/evil-reflecting-shield': [e(BETTER, 'on the saving throw this shield is activated for', { sv: ALL })]`.

**The one defence I could construct, and why it fails.** Someone might reach for the Shove clause to justify `athletics` (Shove is an Athletics action). **Second, separate defect in the same entry (bonus, outside the claim):** the record models only half the printed rule. "If you failed the saving throw, it becomes a success" is `failToSuccess` — which exists in the enum and is already aliased as `F2S` in the script but is unused here. **The `when` string is also wrong**, mildly: "on the check this armor is activated for" — it is a saving throw, not a check, and the armor is not activated *for* a roll; the reaction is triggered *by* an already-failed Fortitude save. CONFIRMED — I tried to refute it and could not.

The head's generic paragraph reads: *"Benefit You gain an item bonus to Fortitude saves and the listed number of temporary Hit Points."* — then a Drawback of −2 to Will/Perception/initiative. That is the whole of the head's own benefit. No degree-of-success clause appears anywhere in it.

The shift is printed only under the grade sub-headings:
- (Lesser), 4 gp: *"The bonus is +1, you gain 5 temporary Hit Points, and the duration is 1 minute."* — nothing more.
- (Moderate), 12 gp: *"The bonus is +2 … 10 minutes."* — nothing more.
- (Greater), 300 gp, level 11: *"When you roll a success on a Fortitude save, you get a critical success instead."*
- (Major), 3,000 gp, level 17: same, plus the critical-failure half.

**The authored value** (`scripts/data/effect-backfill.json` ~line 110304, mirrored into `public/core.json`; source table at `scripts/apply-degree-shifts.mjs:431`) is `{shift:'successToCrit', when:'on a Fortitude save while the mutagen lasts', saves:['fortitude']}` on `juggernaut-mutagen` — level 1, no price. The `when` carries no grade qualifier, so it asserts the shift for *any* juggernaut mutagen while it lasts. The Lesser and Moderate paragraphs quoted above are the specific words that contradicts: they enumerate the grade's entire benefit (bonus, temp HP, duration) and contain no shift.

**Refutations I tested and had to discard:**
1. *Doc comment redefines the field* — no. `ItemBase.degreeShifts` (`src/rules/types.ts:2411`) says shifts "the item grants while in use", and `degreeShiftRecords` (`src/rules/explain.ts:254-274`) applies them to the live sheet for any inventory item that is equipped/worn/invested. It is a mechanic, not a summary surface.
2. *Family-head-as-summary convention* — the app does have one, and it defeats the entry rather than saving it. `situationalBonuses.ts:1791` keys a summary on this same head and states the grade spread explicitly: `"(lesser +1 / moderate +2 / greater +3 / major +4)"`, `"+1 to +4 item (by grade)"`. The degreeShift on the head carries no such qualifier — and note the situational head summary itself lists no degree shift, consistent with the shift being grade-specific.
3. *Owner already ruled* — `docs/mechanic-lanes.md:218`, **Ruling A**: *"umbrella/summary records get no entries and are hidden from pickers."* `juggernaut-mutagen` is an umbrella record by the app's own test; the ruling forbids the entry rather than licensing it.
4. *Redundancy with the grades* — `juggernaut-mutagen-greater` (`apply-degree-shifts.mjs:509`, a later pass) and `-major` (line 432, both halves) already carry the correct entries, so the head adds nothing even where it is right.

- *"juggernaut-mutagen-lesser's grade would inherit it"* is wrong — there is no head→variant inheritance anywhere; `-lesser` is a separate record with no `degreeShifts`. The real exposure is simpler and worse: if `degreeShifts` were ever added to `UMBRELLA_MECHANICAL_FIELDS`, `mechanical()` turns true, the head un-hides, and an unpriced **level-1** item starts granting a level-11 benefit.
